text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High generation latency detected in us-west (/v1/generate). p95 > 2.5s, error rate ~5%. Paging eng-oncall.

maria (oncall): Ack — maria here, taking lead. Triage incoming.

sam (eng): Looking at request routing + kvcache metrics now. Sending logs to the thread.

lee (ops): I can see a surge of prefix cache misses hitting the kv-store around 22:13 UTC. Might be a cold-cache wave from a batch deploy.

maria (oncall): Ops plan: 1) apply fast warmup to hot prefixes, 2) shift ~10% traffic away from us-west to eu-west for low-latency routes, 3) publish statuspage initial update. Draft below — please quick review.

sam (eng): +1 to draft. Also starting a short-lived deployment rollback for a subset to test whether it reduces miss rate.

anya (support): Draft looks fine, but add a line for Dedicated customers — confirm if any impact.

lee (ops): Dedicated capacity unaffected — isolation holds.

textblock: ```Status update (initial): We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent errors for text generation in our us-west region. Some requests may experience slower responses or transient failures. Engineers are applying cache warmups and adjusting routing to mitigate customer impact. We will provide another update within 30 minutes. No data loss is expected.```

tom (legal): Please avoid the term "outage". Replace with "degraded performance". Also OK to state "no data loss expected."

zach (product): Add a short bullet: "Dedicated/reserved capacity customers are not impacted."

maria (oncall): Updated draft with legal + product notes: ready to publish once sam confirms the rollback/warmup results.

sam (eng): Warmup script applied at 22:19 UTC. Preliminary numbers: p95 down from 2.6s -> 1.2s, error rate down from 5% -> 1.1%. Monitoring for 10 minutes.

maria (oncall): :eyes: Good signal. Publishing initial status now. I'll include the ETA note.

maria (oncall): /statuspage post "Initial: We are investigating degraded performance in us-west affecting text generation. Engineers are deploying cache warmups and routing adjustments. Dedicated customers not impacted. Next update in 30m."

anya (support): Posting copy to CS playbook channel so CSMs can triage incoming customer questions.

lee (ops): Rollback of the recent deploy subset completed — no regression observed after rollback.

maria (oncall): Update (22:50 UTC): Improvements holding. p95 ~1.1s, errors ~0.7%. We'll keep monitoring and will post a resolved notice when stable for full traffic.

sam (eng): Monitoring dashboards look green for the affected prefixes. I'm keeping the warmup in place for another 20m.

maria (oncall): Final update: After sustained stability, we restored full routing to us-west at 23:05 UTC. Posting resolved notice.

textblock: ```Resolved: The elevated latency and intermittent errors in us-west have been mitigated. Engineers applied cache warmups and routing adjustments; a targeted rollback was also executed. Service is restored and normal performance has resumed. No data loss occurred. If you continue to experience issues, please open a support ticket.```

maria (oncall): /statuspage post "Resolved: Service restored in us-west. Normal performance resumed. No data loss. If you see any lingering issues, contact support." :thumbsup:

anya (support): Thanks — I've queued a post for the CS team to follow up with customers who opened tickets during the incident.

tom (legal): Approved final wording.

zach (product): Thanks all. Quick retro on the cache warmup cadence next week?

maria (oncall): Agreed — will set a short blameless retro. Closing thread.
